answer: A geochemical attestation scheme ties agent identities to robotic sensing nodes deployed across the ocean floor. To register, an agent must stream real-time reflectance spectra from a localized basalt substrate marked with a photoactive pigment. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying and servicing discrete benthic sampling hardware per identity. However, mineral erosion and biofouling gradually degrade optical fidelity, causing false rejections for legitimate agents.
